trust_decision.summary: parse() feeds an attacker-supplied duration string of any length through several global regex passes (placeholder strip, group/decimal replaceAll, durationRE with \s* and ambiguous \d+\.?\d*|\d*\.?\d+ alternation) with no length bound or linear-time pattern; the cost decision is made solely inside index.js parse().

landing_point.why: durationRE is the only exported-looking regex and the summary names a regex DoS; it is in the only source file.

fix_sites.module_kind: core library function (pre-processing replace chain in the same function)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No plausible dismissal: every route is the single parse() function in index.js; the locale files (locale/*.js) only supply group/decimal strings used by replaceAll, which are literal-string replacements, not regexes.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Locale group/decimal normalisation (e.g. fr/ru group ' ', de/pt/es decimal ',') and digit placeholders like '1_000' or '1 000' must keep parsing; an over-broad fix that rejects spaces/commas or caps length very low would break these and multi-unit strings like '1h30'.
